chunks: “When you hear the crowing of the rooster, then say: ‘Glorified and Holy is the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Your mercy has preceded Your wrath. There is no god but You. Glory be to You, and with Your praise, I have done evil and
‘I have wronged myself, so forgive me’
Indeed, none forgives sins except You.”

key_terms.الذُّنُوبَ: sins, which none forgives except Allah
key_terms.رَبُّ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَ الرُّوحِ: the Lord of the angels and the Spirit
key_terms.رَحْمَتُكَ: Your mercy, described here as preceding wrath
key_terms.سُبُّوحٌ قُدُّوسٌ: utterly glorified and holy, expressions of Allah’s transcendence and purity
key_terms.صُرَاخَ الدِّيكِ: the crowing of the rooster, the occasion for this supplication
key_terms.ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي: I have wronged myself, an admission of personal sin
key_terms.فَاغْفِرْ لِي: so forgive me, a direct plea for divine pardon

ai.seo_question: What should be said when hearing the crowing of a rooster?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific supplication to be recited upon hearing the crowing of a rooster. It combines glorification of Allah, acknowledgment of His mercy, confession of wrongdoing, and seeking forgiveness from Him alone.
